property_summary: For any deposited amount, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance must be fully drained (zero wei); the mutant always leaves 1 wei behind.

For any contract balance b, after the owner calls withdrawAll the remaining balance is strictly below 1 wei, so a subsequent owner withdraw(1) must revert; the mutant leaves exactly 1 wei behind, making withdraw(1) succeed.

For any admissible balance b >= 1 wei, after the owner calls withdrawAll() the contract retains less than 1 wei (it is completely drained); the mutant always retains exactly 1 wei, so for every admissible b the assertion address(c).balance < 1 wei fails on the mutant.
For any admissibly-funded balance, after the owner calls withdrawAll() the contract's ether balance is exactly zero; the mutant always leaves 1 wei behind, breaking this for every balance >= 1.

For any withdrawal amount, calling withdraw as the owner must transfer that amount out so the contract's balance decreases by exactly the amount (ends at zero when it held only that amount); the mutant transfers to itself, leaving the balance unchanged.

For any amount, after the owner withdraws that amount the contract's balance must decrease by exactly that amount (be zero if it held only that amount); the mutant self-transfers, leaving the balance unchanged.
For any withdrawable amount, the owner's balance must increase by that amount (funds leave the contract to the caller); the mutant pays the contract itself so the owner's balance stays unchanged.

For any admissible amount, an owner withdrawal must pay the CALLER, so a counterparty that reverts on receiving funds causes withdraw to fail in C; the mutant pays the contract itself, whose fallback accepts, so withdraw succeeds.

For any admissible amount, funding the contract with that amount and calling withdraw(amount) as owner must leave address(c).balance reduced by exactly that amount (to zero here); the mutant pays the contract itself so the balance stays unchanged.
Only the owner can drain the contract: after a non-owner calls withdrawAll, address(c).balance must be unchanged; the mutant lets any caller drain it.

For every non-owner actor and any balance, calling withdrawAll must never change address(c).balance — only the owner may drain it — but the mutant lets any caller drain the contract, emptying it for some non-owner.

For any caller other than the owner, withdrawAll must revert (access control), regardless of contract balance; the mutant lets a non-owner successfully drain, so it returns without reverting for some (actor, amount) input.

For any non-owner caller and any funding amount, withdrawAll must revert (access control) and leave the contract's balance untouched; the mutant lets a non-owner successfully drain the balance, returning ok==true and emptying it.

For any non-owner actor and any deposit, calling withdrawAll must revert and leave the contract's balance intact (only the owner may drain); the mutant lets a non-owner successfully drain the deposited funds, so the call succeeds and the balance drops to zero.

For any admissible input, after the owner funds c and calls withdrawAll, the contract's full balance is drained so address(c).balance == 0; the mutant transfers 0 and leaves funds behind, breaking the rule when balance > 0.

For any positive amount, after funding c with that amount and the owner calling withdrawAll, c's balance is fully drained (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant transfers 0 and leaves the funds behind.

For any amount 1 <= amount <= contract balance, calling withdraw(amount) as owner reduces the contract's balance by exactly amount; the mutant transfers one wei less, so the balance is amount-1 higher than expected.
A non-owner's call to withdraw must revert (only the owner can withdraw funds), so withdraw invoked by any account other than the owner never succeeds.
